arxiv-2106-00616.title: Halfspace depth for general measures: The ray basis theorem and its consequences
arxiv-2106-00616.creator: Petra Laketa, Stanislav Nagy
arxiv-2106-00616.description: Abstract . The halfspace depth is a prominent tool of nonparametric multivariate analysis. The upper level sets of the depth, termed the trimmed regions of a measure, serve as a natural generalization of the quantiles and inter-quantile regions to higher-dimensional spaces. The smallest non-empty trimmed region, coined the halfspace median of a measure, generalizes the median.

arxiv-2310-11640.title: Free-text Keystroke Authentication using Transformers: A Comparative Study of Architectures and Loss Functions
arxiv-2310-11640.creator: Saleh Momeni, Bagher BabaAli*
arxiv-2310-11640.description: Abstract Keystroke biometrics is a promising approach for user identification and verification, leveraging the unique patterns in individuals’ typing behavior. In this paper, we propose a Transformer-based network that employs self-attention to extract informative features from keystroke sequences, surpassing the performance of traditional Recurrent Neural Networks.

arxiv-2405-08452.title: Far-from-equilibrium complex landscapes
arxiv-2405-08452.creator: Laura Guislain, Eric Bertin
arxiv-2405-08452.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Laura Guislain, Eric Bertin. Systems with a complex dynamics like glasses or models of biological evolution are often pictured in terms of complex landscapes, with a large number of possible collective states. We show on the example of a stochastic spin model with non-reciprocal and heterogeneous interactions how the complex landscape notion can be generalized far from equilibrium, where collective states may exhibit spontaneous oscillations, often hidden by the presence of disorder.

arxiv-2407-19276.title: Linear maps preserving ℓ p \ell_{p} -norm parallel vectors
arxiv-2407-19276.creator: Chi-Kwong Li, Ming-Cheng Tsai, Ya-Shu Wang and Ngai-Ching Wong
arxiv-2407-19276.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Chi-Kwong Li, Ming-Cheng Tsai, Ya-Shu Wang and Ngai-Ching Wong. Two vectors 𝐱 , 𝐲 \mathbf{x},\mathbf{y} in a normed vector space are parallel if there is a scalar μ \mu with | μ | = 1 |\mu|=1 such that ‖ 𝐱 + μ ​ 𝐲 ‖ = ‖ 𝐱 ‖ + ‖ 𝐲 ‖ \|\mathbf{x}+\mu\mathbf{y}\|=\|\mathbf{x}\|+\|\mathbf{y}\| ; they form a triangle equality attaining (TEA) pair if ‖ 𝐱 + 𝐲 ‖ = ‖ 𝐱 ‖ + ‖ 𝐲 ‖ \|\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{y}\|=\|\mathbf{x}\|+\|\mathbf{y}\| .

arxiv-2504-13733.title: Dynamic Regularized CBDT: Variance-Calibrated Causal Boosting for Interpretable Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
arxiv-2504-13733.creator: Yichen Liu
arxiv-2504-13733.description: Abstract Heterogeneous treatment effect estimation in high-stakes applications demands models that simultaneously optimize precision, interpretability, and calibration. Many existing tree-based causal inference techniques, however, exhibit high estimation errors when applied to observational data because they struggle to capture complex interactions among factors and rely on static regularization schemes.

arxiv-2507-14933.title: Simple model of violent relaxation of a spherical stellar system
arxiv-2507-14933.creator: V. Yu. Terebizh
arxiv-2507-14933.description: Abstract A spherical system with arbitrary mean velocities in the radial and transverse directions, but with zero dispersion of radial velocities, is considered as a model describing the violent relaxation of star clusters and galaxies. The model allows to reduce the infinite chain of Jeans’ equations of moments to just three hydrodynamic equations.

arxiv-2510-15206.title: Effective string theory on a torus: the 3d Ising domain wall
arxiv-2510-15206.creator: David Lima, J. M. Viana Parente Lopes, José Matos, Joao Penedones
arxiv-2510-15206.description: Abstract We use effective string theory (EST) to describe a toroidal 2d domain wall embedded in a 3d torus. In particular, we compute the free energy of the domain wall in an expansion in inverse powers of the area, up to the second non-universal order that involves the Wilson coefficient γ 3 \gamma_{3} .

arxiv-2511-18194.title: Agent-as-a-Graph: Knowledge Graph-Based Tool and Agent Retrieval for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
arxiv-2511-18194.creator: Faheem Nizar, Elias Lumer, Anmol Gulati, Pradeep Honaganahalli Basavaraju, and Vamse Kumar Subbiah Commercial Technology and Innovation Office, PricewaterhouseCoopers, U.S.
arxiv-2511-18194.description: Abstract Recent advances in Large Language Model Multi-Agent Systems enable scalable orchestration and retrieval of specialized, parallelized subagents, each equipped with hundreds or thousands of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and tools. However, existing agent, MCP, and retrieval methods typically match queries against a single agent description, obscuring fine-grained tool capabilities of each agent, resulting in suboptimal agent selection.

pmc-10644594.title: Evaluating residual tumor after neoadjuvant chemotherapy for muscle-invasive urothelial bladder cancer: diagnostic performance and outcomes using biparametric vs. multiparametric MRI
pmc-10644594.creator: Sungmin Woo, Anton S Becker, Jeeban P Das, Soleen Ghafoor, Yuki Arita, Nicole Benfante, Natalie Gangai, Min Yuen Teo, Alvin C Goh, Hebert A Vargas
pmc-10644594.description: BackgroundNeoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) before radical cystectomy is standard of care in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC). Response assessment after NAC is important but suboptimal using CT. We assessed MRI without vs. with intravenous contrast (biparametric [BP] vs. multiparametric [MP]) for identifying residual disease on cystectomy and explored its prognostic role.

pmc-10745781.title: Associations of Plastic Bottle Exposure with Infant Growth, Fecal Microbiota, and Short-Chain Fatty Acids
pmc-10745781.creator: Curtis Tilves, Heather Jianbo Zhao, Moira K. Differding, Mingyu Zhang, Tiange Liu, Cathrine Hoyo, Truls Østbye, Sara E. Benjamin-Neelon, Noel T. Mueller
pmc-10745781.description: Background/Objectives: Murine models show that plastics, via their chemical constituents (e.g., phthalates), influence microbiota, metabolism, and growth. However, research on plastics in humans is lacking. Here, we examine how the frequency of plastic bottle exposure is associated with fecal microbiota, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), and anthropometry in the first year of life.

pmc-11365535.title: Hepatocyte-Specific Yap1 Knockout Maintained the Liver Homeostasis of Lipid Metabolism in Mice
pmc-11365535.creator: Caige Li, Yu Xue, Yiwei Liu, Kangning Zheng, Yuting Gao, Yi Gong, Junlan Lu, Yuman Zhang, Jingmin Ji, Zhiqin Zhang, Xinli Shi
pmc-11365535.description: IntroductionYes-associated protein 1 (YAP1) is a crucial molecule in the Hippo pathway. The impact of hepatocyte-specific Yap1 knockout (Yap1LKO) on hepatic lipid droplets (LD) and pePLIN2 in metabolic fatty liver has not been reported. This study aims to explore whether Yap1LKO could offer a protective effect in a liver injury model.

pmc-11387636.title: Genetic homogeneity and weak signatures of local adaptation in the marine mussel Mytilus chilensis
pmc-11387636.creator: Nicolás I Segovia, Diana Coral-Santacruz, Pilar A Haye
pmc-11387636.description: The natural populations of the marine mussel Mytilus chilensis and the associated aquaculture industry forms a sensitive social-ecological system that relies on the released propagules for cultivation in the highly heterogeneous environment (temperature, productivity, and salinity) of northern Patagonia (42–44 °S). We assessed spatial genetic structure, signals of local adaptation, and population assignment of M.

pmc-11651171.title: Causes, Solutions and Health Inequalities: Comparing Perspectives of Professional Stakeholders and Community Participants Experiencing Low Income and Poor Health in London
pmc-11651171.creator: Neil McHugh, Rachel Baker, Cam Donaldson, Ahalya Bala, Marta Mojarrieta, Gregory White, Olga Biosca
pmc-11651171.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundEngaging with the public can influence policy decisions, particularly towards more radical policy change. While established research exists exploring public perceptions on causes of health inequalities, much less exists on how to tackle health inequalities in the UK.

pmc-11655892.title: The landscape in telomere related gene prognostic signature for survival and medication treatment effectiveness prediction in hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-11655892.creator: Kai Zhou, Xingyu Liu, Mingda Wang, Jinjiang Duan, Xu Zhao, Hanjun Yin
pmc-11655892.description: ObjectiveTelomeres, made of repetitive DNA sequences and shelterin complexes, which were found at the ends of chromosomes and had been extensively studied in cancer research. However, in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) was still relatively scarce. In this study, we investigated the correlation between telomerase-related genes (TRGs) and the prognosis and immunotherapy of HCC patients to enhance clinical outcomes.

pmc-12656300.title: Advancing Medical Training with Mixed Reality and Haptic Feedback Simulator for Acupuncture Needling
pmc-12656300.creator: Kasunika Guruge, H. M. K. K. M. B. Herath, Nuwan Madusanka, Hi-Joon Park, Chang-Su Na, Myunggi Yi, Byeong-il Lee
pmc-12656300.description: Traditional acupuncture training often lacks consistent, objective feedback, while current extended reality (XR) solutions rarely include quantitative assessment. This study developed and evaluated a feedback-enabled mixed reality (MR) acupuncture simulator to improve skill acquisition through depth-responsive guidance. The system, used on Microsoft HoloLens 2, combines a MetaHuman-based virtual patient with expert-designed acupoint geometries.

pmc-12951641.title: Behavioral variability and neural cross-frequency coupling distinguish working memory maintenance from manipulation
pmc-12951641.creator: Yingzhe Li, Romy Lorenz, Guang Ouyang
pmc-12951641.description: Working memory (WM) is typically understood to comprise two core components: maintenance (short-term retention) and manipulation (active processing of information). However, many existing WM tasks are composite in design, involving both components and even other cognitive processes or constructs. Explicit characterization of the two components in terms of cross-individual variability in both behavioral performance and neural correlates remains limited.

pmc-13092282.title: Advances in Artificial Intelligence‐Based Liver‐Related Semantic Segmentation Techniques and Applications Using CT Imaging
pmc-13092282.creator: Jun Pu, Xuan Wang, Liang Zhu, Jie Pan
pmc-13092282.description: Background and AimsArtificial intelligence (AI)‐assisted semantic segmentation of liver computed tomography (CT) images has important clinical value in disease assessment, surgical planning, treatment evaluation, and longitudinal monitoring. This review aims to summarize the current clinical applications and recent technical advances in AI‐based liver‐related semantic segmentation on CT.

pmc-13427732.title: Integrating validated scores with clinical parameters to predict NIV weaning outcomes: a prospective study in the respiratory ICU

pmc-13499229.title: Overcoming the Dexter distance constraint: a relay strategy for asymmetric photocatalysis
pmc-13499229.creator: Hao Zeng, Jie Wu
pmc-13499229.description: onal asymmetric EnT catalysis, a chiral catalyst is often introduced to bind the substrate, lower its triplet energy and induce stereocontrol. However, triplet-energy matching alone is insufficient. According to Dexter theory, efficient EnT requires close spatial proximity and orbital overlap between the donor and acceptor, with the transfer rate decaying exponentially as distance increases [5].

pmc-13522156.title: Evaluating economic and health-system associations of a national public health legal framework: evidence from China’s basic medical and health care and health promotion law
pmc-13522156.creator: Peiran Lu
pmc-13522156.description: BackgroundFramework health legislation is increasingly used to codify government responsibility, health-promotion duties, and accountability for basic services, yet it is difficult to identify whether such laws produce measurable economic and health effects. China’s Basic Medical and Health Care and Health Promotion Law, effective June 2020, consolidated these duties in a single national statute.

pmc-13617661.title: Long-term growth in child mental health expenditures, 2004-2023
pmc-13617661.creator: Joshua Breslau, Dar Alon, Alyssa Burnett, Jonathan Cantor, Ryan K McBain, Ateev Mehrotra, Bradley D Stein, Fang Zhang, Hao Yu
pmc-13617661.description: IntroductionInvestment in mental health treatment for children has grown substantially, but whether this reflects more treatment recipients, higher spending per user, or both has not been examined. To estimate trends in mental health expenditures, probability of use and expenditures per user for US children aged 2-17 from 2004 to 2023.

(a) Findings.— Congress finds the following: (1) Internet gambling is primarily funded through personal use of payment system instruments, credit cards, and wire transfers. (2) The National Gambling Impact Study Commission in 1999 recommended the passage.
